walk.definition: To move forward on foot at a steady, normal pace.
walk.exampleUsage: We walk to the neighborhood mosque together every evening.

run.definition: To move quickly on foot so that both feet briefly leave the ground.
run.exampleUsage: The boys like to run across the grass in the park.

jog.definition: To run at a slow, steady pace for exercise.
jog.exampleUsage: He goes to the park to jog for thirty minutes every morning.

sprint.definition: To run at full speed over a short distance.
sprint.exampleUsage: The runners had to sprint during the final meters of the race.

march.definition: To walk with regular, firm, and measured steps.
march.exampleUsage: The scouts march in a straight line across the field.

stroll.definition: To walk in a slow, relaxed way for pleasure.
stroll.exampleUsage: After dinner, the family took a quiet stroll through the garden.

hike.definition: To go for a long walk in the countryside or mountains.
hike.exampleUsage: They plan to hike along the mountain trail this weekend.

trek.definition: To make a long, challenging journey on foot.
trek.exampleUsage: The explorers had to trek across rugged hills for three days.

pace.definition: To walk back and forth across a room, often while thinking or waiting.
pace.exampleUsage: He began to pace the hallway while waiting for the exam results.

stride.definition: To walk forward with long, confident steps.
stride.exampleUsage: We watched the speaker stride confidently toward the stage.

jump.definition: To push yourself off the ground into the air using your legs and feet.
jump.exampleUsage: The child tried to jump over the small puddle of water.

hop.definition: To jump lightly on one foot or with both feet together.
hop.exampleUsage: We watched a small bird hop from branch to branch.

skip.definition: To move forward lightly by stepping and hopping on each foot in turn.
skip.exampleUsage: The young children skip happily along the garden path.

leap.definition: To jump high or a long way with great energy.
leap.exampleUsage: The deer was able to leap gracefully over the low fence.

bounce.definition: To spring back up quickly after hitting a surface.
bounce.exampleUsage: Throw the rubber ball on the court and watch it bounce.

climb.definition: To go up a hill, ladder, or tree using your feet and hands.
climb.exampleUsage: The workers had to climb a tall ladder to fix the roof.

crawl.definition: To move forward close to the ground on your hands and knees.
crawl.exampleUsage: The baby learned to crawl across the living room rug.

scale.definition: To climb up to the top of a steep wall, cliff, or mountain.
scale.exampleUsage: Experienced climbers use ropes to scale the rocky cliff.

vault.definition: To leap over an obstacle while supporting yourself with your hands or a pole.
vault.exampleUsage: He used both hands to vault over the wooden gate.

hurdle.definition: To jump over a barrier or frame while running at high speed.
hurdle.exampleUsage: Track athletes train hard to hurdle smoothly without slowing down.

swim.definition: To move through water by moving your arms and legs.
swim.exampleUsage: My brother taught me how to swim in the pool last summer.

float.definition: To rest or move gently on the surface of water without sinking.
float.exampleUsage: Dry wooden branches float easily on the surface of the river.

dive.definition: To jump or plunge headfirst into deep water.
dive.exampleUsage: Swimmers dive into the deep end of the pool at the start of the race.

paddle.definition: To move a small boat or kayak through water using a paddle.
paddle.exampleUsage: We used wooden oars to paddle the canoe across the calm lake.

wade.definition: To walk slowly through shallow water near the shore.
wade.exampleUsage: The fishermen wade into the shallow water to pull in their nets.

splash.definition: To cause water to fly around in drops with a noisy sound.
splash.exampleUsage: The children love to splash water on a warm summer afternoon.

surf.definition: To ride toward the shore on the crest of ocean waves using a board.
surf.exampleUsage: Early in the morning, athletes gather at the coast to surf the waves.

row.definition: To propel a boat through water using oars.
row.exampleUsage: It takes strong arms to row a wooden boat against the current.

sail.definition: To travel across water in a boat or ship powered by the wind.
sail.exampleUsage: Merchants used wooden ships to sail across the sea.

snorkel.definition: To swim near the surface of the water while breathing through a curved tube.
snorkel.exampleUsage: Visitors snorkel near the reef to see colorful fish.

dance.definition: To move your body and feet rhythmically, often during a celebration.
dance.exampleUsage: The guests gathered in a circle to perform a traditional folk dance.

spin.definition: To turn around and around quickly on one spot.
spin.exampleUsage: Push the wooden top and watch it spin on the table.

twirl.definition: To turn or spin something around lightly and quickly.
twirl.exampleUsage: The performer learned to twirl the baton without dropping it.

slide.definition: To move smoothly along a flat or slippery surface.
slide.exampleUsage: Be careful not to slide on the wet tile floor.

roll.definition: To move along a surface by turning over and over.
roll.exampleUsage: The round orange began to roll across the kitchen table.

tumble.definition: To fall suddenly and roll downward in an uncontrolled way.
tumble.exampleUsage: Loose stones began to tumble down the steep hillside.

swing.definition: To move smoothly backward and forward from a fixed point.
swing.exampleUsage: The children take turns on the park swing after school.

somersault.definition: To roll your body forward or backward in a complete circle heels over head.
somersault.exampleUsage: The gymnast practiced a forward somersault on the soft mat.

cartwheel.definition: To turn sideways in a circle using your hands and feet like the spokes of a wheel.
cartwheel.exampleUsage: The young acrobat did a neat cartwheel across the gym mat.

pirouette.definition: To make a rapid full turn of the body on the point of the toe or ball of the foot.
pirouette.exampleUsage: The skater finished the routine with a balanced pirouette.

stand.definition: To be in an upright position on your feet.
stand.exampleUsage: Please stand up to greet our guests when they enter the room.

sit.definition: To rest your weight on your lower body on a chair or the ground.
sit.exampleUsage: Come inside and sit on the sofa beside your grandfather.

lie-down.definition: To put your body flat in a horizontal position to rest or sleep.
lie-down.exampleUsage: If you have a headache, lie down in a quiet room for a while.

kneel.definition: To rest or support your body weight on one or both knees.
kneel.exampleUsage: Gardeners often kneel on a soft pad while planting flowers.

crouch.definition: To lower your body close to the ground by bending your knees and back.
crouch.exampleUsage: He had to crouch down to look under the low wooden table.

bend.definition: To curve or incline your body or a joint downward or forward.
bend.exampleUsage: Bend your knees when lifting a heavy box to protect your back.

stretch.definition: To extend your arms, legs, or body to full length to loosen your muscles.
stretch.exampleUsage: Always stretch your leg muscles before and after running.

lean.definition: To incline or rest your body against a wall or object for support.
lean.exampleUsage: Do not lean against the freshly painted wall.

squat.definition: To bend your knees deeply so your body sits close to your heels.
squat.exampleUsage: He did ten slow squat exercises during his morning workout.

balance.definition: To keep your body steady and upright without falling to either side.
balance.exampleUsage: The child tried to balance on the narrow wooden beam.
